_comment: Configuration of runtime/data-probe/data_probe.py (contract: runtime/data-probe/README.md). A case file: keep it outside the kit, beside the case's notes. Fictional example: the ACME orders system - a local copy, a read replica reached through the engine's own client, and a disposable scratch copy. Keys starting with _ are notes. NO SECRET EVER GOES HERE: a password comes from an environment variable named in connect_env, or the login uses integrated authentication.
_require_proof: true makes a target without read_only_proof a configuration error (the sqlite adapter has a built-in proof)

orders-copy._comment: A copy of the orders database file, opened read-only by URI; the adapter's own test write proves it.
orders-copy.database: <path to a copy of the orders database file>

orders-replica._comment: The engine's own command-line client. The SQL goes on its standard input; the client inherits this process's environment, so its credential variable or integrated authentication works and nothing secret is on its command line.
orders-replica.session_prelude: <the engine's statement that makes this session read-only>

read_only_proof.statement: UPDATE orders SET status = status WHERE 1 = 0

lexical._comment: Declare what the engine does; an option left out is checked both ways (more refusals, never fewer).

orders-dbapi._comment: A DB-API 2.0 module the case installed (the kit installs none). connect holds no secret; connect_env names the variable that does.
orders-dbapi.session_prelude: <the engine's statement that makes this session read-only>

read_only_proof.statement: UPDATE orders SET status = status WHERE 1 = 0

orders-scratch._comment: A disposable copy: the only kind of target --allow-write accepts.
